newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt to pursue open sky agreements - Peters.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt to pursue open sky agreements - Peters.

text.p: The New Zealand government was keen to pursue bilateral open skies agreements in the Asia-Pacific region and beyond, Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday.
"Removing restrictions on air services to and from New Zealand is important for reducing barriers to trade and tourism," Peters told a business breakfast meeting.
"To this end, the government remains committed to reciprocal liberalisation where possible."
Peters said New Zealand was a small country in a global economy, and it had to be open and outward-looking if it was to be successful. The government was committed to innovative reform, he said.

The key to maintaining an open, internationally competitive economy would be stable macroeconomic policies; deregulated, competitive and open markets; quality public services provided as efficiently as possible; and the lowest possible tax rates.
